name: Vote Leave

summary.text: Vote Leave Ltd was the designated lead campaign for leaving the EU in the 2016 referendum. On 17 July 2018 the Electoral Commission found that Vote Leave and Darren Grimes had broken electoral law: Grimes's and BeLeave's spending was incurred under a common plan with Vote Leave, taking Vote Leave's spending to £7,449,079.34 against a £7 million limit. Vote Leave was fined £61,000, Grimes £20,000 and Veterans for Britain £250, and the Commission referred Grimes and Vote Leave's responsible person David Halsall to the Metropolitan Police. Vote Leave dropped its appeal in March 2019; Grimes won his appeal in July 2019; the Met closed its investigation without charges.

facts.claim: The Electoral Commission concluded on 17 July 2018 that all of Darren Grimes's and BeLeave's spending on referendum campaigning was incurred under a common plan with Vote Leave, and that Vote Leave's referendum spending was £7,449,079.34, exceeding its statutory limit of £7 million.
facts.quote: Vote Leave's referendum spending was £7,449,079.34, exceeding its statutory spending limit of £7 million

facts.claim: The Commission fined Vote Leave £61,000, Darren Grimes £20,000 and Veterans for Britain £250, and found Vote Leave had returned an incomplete and inaccurate spending report, with £234,501 reported incorrectly and invoices missing for £12,849.99 of spending.
facts.quote: the levels of fines are £61,000 for Vote Leave, £20,000 for Mr Grimes and £250 for Veterans for Britain

facts.claim: The investigation mainly concerned five payments made in June 2016 to the Canadian firm Aggregate IQ; BeLeave spent more than £675,000 with AggregateIQ under a common plan with Vote Leave, which the Commission said should have been declared by Vote Leave.
facts.quote: mainly concerned five payments made in June 2016 to a Canadian data analytics firm called Aggregate IQ

facts.claim: The Commission referred David Halsall, the responsible person for Vote Leave, and Darren Grimes to the Metropolitan Police in relation to false declarations of campaign spending; the Met later closed its investigation into Vote Leave and Grimes.
